definitions.explanation: Fish or other seafood that has been preserved by drying, typically split open and sun-dried or wind-dried. A traditional Japanese food preparation method.

examples.japanese: {干物|ひもの}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{焼|や}く→焼く：01123_yaku⟧。
{朝|あさ}ごはん⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{鯵|あじ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{干物|ひもの}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べた→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: I had dried horse mackerel for breakfast.

examples.japanese: ⟦{海沿|うみぞ}い→海沿い：27984_umizoi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{町|まち}→町：00613_machi⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{店先|みせさき}→店先：20728_misesaki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{干物|ひもの}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{並|なら}べられ→並べる：01091_naraberu⟧、⟦{潮|しお}→潮：13369_shio⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{香|かお}り→香り：00189_kaori⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{一緒|いっしょ}→一緒：02848_issho⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{旅行者|りょこうしゃ}→旅行者：22927_ryokousha⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{迎|むか}えて→迎える：01193_mukaeru⟧⟦くれる→くれる：00724_kureru⟧。
examples.english: In the coastal town, dried fish are laid out at storefronts, welcoming travelers along with the scent of the sea.

notes:
COMMON PATTERNS:
{干|ひ} (dry) + ⟦{物|もの}→物：02259_mono⟧ (thing). Literally "dried thing."

USAGE:
{干物|ひもの} primarily refers to dried fish, which is a staple of traditional Japanese breakfasts. Common types include {鯵|あじ} (horse mackerel), ⟦{鯖|さば}→鯖：08655_saba⟧ (mackerel), and {鰯|いわし} (sardine). The fish is typically split open ({開|ひら}き), salted, and dried. {干物|ひもの} is often associated with seaside towns and ⟦{旅館|りょかん}→旅館：01049_ryokan⟧ (Japanese inns). Colloquially, {干物|ひもの}⟦{女|おんな}→女：00559_onna⟧ ("dried fish woman") is slang for a woman who stays home and lives a lazy lifestyle.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {干物|ひもの}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{焼|や}く→焼く：01123_yaku⟧: to grill dried fish
- {鯵|あじ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{干物|ひもの}: dried horse mackerel
- {干物|ひもの}⟦{屋|や}→〜屋：03096_ya⟧: dried fish shop
- ⟦{自家製|じかせい}→自家製：13947_jikasei⟧{干物|ひもの}: homemade dried fish
